title: The complexity bound conjecture for S(e,23,e)-adic languages
source: Thomas Garrity and Otto Vaughn Osterman, “On the Factor Complexity Associated with a Family of Multidimensional Continued Fraction Algorithms”, arXiv:2410.02032 (2026; Combinatorics and Number Theory 15:4, 2026), Conjecture 53. https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.02032

significance.root_decision: For every directive sequence over the two substitutions of the TRIP-map family S(e,23,e), the factor complexity of the S-adic language satisfies p(n) ≤ 3n for every n ≥ 1; the bound is attained. The source proves the analogous bound for the family (e,e,e), outlines the method for (e,23,e) in its Section 10 with Propositions 69–71 stated without proof, and names the remaining work: characterize the bispecial words and control their lengths. The proof does this: every double-Gauss block is a 3-free word followed by a single 3, which gives unique parsing and the exact extension sets in both directions (the source's Proposition 71, here proved); the bispecial factors are classified into 23 types; and a new cross-age matching between bispecials of different levels controls their total extension count. Lean defines the two substitutions, the directive applied with d(0) outermost as the source's Definition 14 requires, the language as the factor closure of all images, and the complexity as the number of factors of length n, and proves the bound for every directive sequence, including degenerate ones such as the all-S1 sequence.
significance.caveat: The conjecture's surrounding text mentions twins and conjugates of S(e,23,e); those transfer by the source's proved Propositions 45 and 47 (the final check verified directly that each of the 5 conjugates and 6 twins in the source's appendix is a letter-permuted or reversed copy) and are not formalized. A specialist would see the result as the authors' announced strategy carried to completion, with one new ingredient (the cross-age matching); cross-model reviewer: not routine 0.55, at the floor root uses for counting; the final checker judged it a real step and asked for modest wording. The Lean was started by a GPT-6.1 Sol lane and finished by a Claude Opus 5.5 lane (4,097 lines in 23 modules); because GPT-6.1 Sol hit its usage limit, the final check was by a separate Claude Opus 5.5 lane, the same model family as the packager (the cross-model review is the Opus pre-Lean review of a Sol proof).

root_basis: Root (Claude Opus 5.5) extracted the 23 modules from the appendix into an empty directory, rebuilt and kernel-checked them (all exit 0, axioms exactly the allowed three for both endpoints, no forbidden tokens), and compared S0, S1, subst, prefImage, lang, complexity, Conjecture53 and the final theorem with the endpoint written by the Claude Opus referee: identical (S0 and S1 written by cases instead of vector notation).
